AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is soil erosion? (1 mark)
   A. The washing or blowing away of top soil
   B. Watering the garden
   C. Adding manure to soil
   D. Planting trees

2. Which is a benefit of compost to sandy soil? (1 mark)
   A. It helps the soil to hold water
   B. It makes the soil more sandy
   C. It removes all nutrients
   D. It makes the soil disappear

3. Why is meat kept out of a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. It turns into plastic
   B. It attracts rats and flies and smells bad
   C. It kills the soil
   D. It makes the compost too dry

4. What does soil conservation mean? (1 mark)
   A. Selling soil to other farmers
   B. Looking after soil so that it stays healthy and stays in place
   C. Covering the soil with plastic
   D. Digging up all the soil on a farm

5. Which is a benefit of drip irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. The leaves get very wet
   B. More weeds grow
   C. Fewer weeds grow between plants
   D. Water is wasted

6. Why do children need an adult when cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Adults always cook faster
   B. Fire is not dangerous
   C. Children cannot lift a spoon
   D. Fuels and fire can burn people

7. Why does a lid on a pot save fuel? (1 mark)
   A. It keeps the heat in so food cooks faster
   B. It stops the food from cooking
   C. It cools the food
   D. It makes the pot lighter

8. What should you do if you smell gas in the kitchen? (1 mark)
   A. Switch on many lights
   B. Close the cylinder valve and open windows and doors
   C. Light a match to see
   D. Cover your nose and cook

9. What does sowing mean? (1 mark)
   A. Storing seeds
   B. Putting seeds into the soil so they can grow
   C. Watering a crop
   D. Cutting a crop

10. How do you know millet is ready to harvest? (1 mark)
   A. The heads turn brown and the grains are hard
   B. The seeds are wet
   C. The plants are green and soft
   D. The plant flowers

11. Which site is suitable for planting a fruit tree? (1 mark)
   A. A deep shade under big trees
   B. Inside a building
   C. A flooded area
   D. A sunny place with space to spread

12. At what depth should the seedling be planted? (1 mark)
   A. Very deep
   B. Upside down
   C. The same depth as it was in the bag
   D. On top of the ground

13. About how big should a planting hole for a fruit tree be? (1 mark)
   A. About half a metre wide and deep
   B. 10 cm wide only
   C. About 1 cm
   D. As big as a football field

14. What is the young one of a sheep called? (1 mark)
   A. Calf
   B. Lamb
   C. Kid
   D. Foal

15. What is the meat from cattle called? (1 mark)
   A. Pork
   B. Chicken
   C. Beef
   D. Mutton

16. What is leather made from? (1 mark)
   A. Eggs
   B. Animal hides and skins
   C. Feathers
   D. Wool only

17. Which nutrient do body-building foods supply? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Fibre only
   C. Protein
   D. Salt

18. Which of these is an energy-giving fat? (1 mark)
   A. Beans
   B. Oranges
   C. Cooking oil
   D. Spinach

19. Why should potatoes be cut into pieces of equal size before boiling? (1 mark)
   A. To make them cold
   B. They cook at the same time
   C. To make them bigger
   D. To waste time

20. Which way should you open a lid on a hot pot? (1 mark)
   A. Away from your face
   B. Under water
   C. Straight toward your face
   D. Fast and close

21. What should you do first for a small burn? (1 mark)
   A. Cool it under running clean water for at least ten minutes
   B. Cover with toothpaste
   C. Ignore it
   D. Put butter on it

22. How can you tell that water is boiling? (1 mark)
   A. The water is still
   B. The water is cold
   C. The water is blue
   D. Big bubbles rise quickly and steam comes off

23. What should be placed under a tippy tap? (1 mark)
   A. A plant only
   B. A radio
   C. A basin or a soak pit
   D. A bed

24. What should you use to wash your hands? (1 mark)
   A. Only dry cloth
   B. Dirty water
   C. Mud
   D. Soap and clean water

25. Why should dusters and mops be washed after use? (1 mark)
   A. To make them heavy
   B. To make them smell
   C. So they wear out
   D. So they do not spread dirt and germs

26. What should you wear when handling rubbish? (1 mark)
   A. Sandals only
   B. Only a hat
   C. Gloves
   D. Nothing

27. How can a dustpan be improvised? (1 mark)
   A. Cut a jerrican or flat tin
   B. Use a rope
   C. Use a sack
   D. Use a chair

28. What is domestic hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking meals
   B. Growing food
   C. Washing your own body
   D. Keeping the home and its surroundings clean

29. Which PPE keeps dust from being breathed in? (1 mark)
   A. Headgear
   B. Overall
   C. Gumboots
   D. Dust mask

30. In long and short tacking, the pattern is (1 mark)
   A. A long stitch followed by a short stitch
   B. All stitches short
   C. All gaps long
   D. No stitch

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Describe how to mop a floor. (4 marks)

32. Explain how good personal hygiene helps prevent diseases such as diarrhoea. (4 marks)

33. List three safety rules when harvesting fruit. (3 marks)

34. Name two things that should never be put in a compost heap and say why. (2 marks)

35. Describe how to clean canvas shoes. (4 marks)

36. Name two types of tacking stitches and describe each. (3 marks)

37. Plan a balanced supper using local foods and name the group of each food. (3 marks)

38. Explain the meaning of domestic hygiene. (2 marks)

39. What should be done with a paper dust mask that is dirty? (2 marks)

40. Why do some fruit trees take longer to give fruit than others? (3 marks)

41. Name the three main food groups and one example of each. (3 marks)

42. Compare a watering can with drip irrigation. (4 marks)

43. Describe how to make a simple trellis for passion fruit. (4 marks)

44. Why must a passion fruit plant have a trellis? (2 marks)

45. Explain why vegetables and fruits should be eaten every day. (3 marks)

46. Name four fuels used for cooking in homes. (2 marks)

47. Explain the meaning of personal hygiene. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — The washing or blowing away of top soil
   Bare soil can be carried away by rain or wind.

2. A — It helps the soil to hold water
   Compost holds water like a sponge.

3. B — It attracts rats and flies and smells bad
   Meat and fatty food attract pests and create a bad smell.

4. B — Looking after soil so that it stays healthy and stays in place
   Soil conservation protects the soil from being washed away and from losing its plant food.

5. C — Fewer weeds grow between plants
   The soil between plants stays dry so fewer weeds grow.

6. D — Fuels and fire can burn people
   Adults can guide and help prevent accidents.

7. A — It keeps the heat in so food cooks faster
   Less heat escapes so less fuel is used.

8. B — Close the cylinder valve and open windows and doors
   Fire near a gas leak can cause an explosion.

9. B — Putting seeds into the soil so they can grow
   Sowing is planting seeds.

10. A — The heads turn brown and the grains are hard
   Ripe grain is hard and dry.

11. D — A sunny place with space to spread
   Fruit trees need light and space.

12. C — The same depth as it was in the bag
   Planting too deep can rot the stem.

13. A — About half a metre wide and deep
   The hole gives roots space in loose soil.

14. B — Lamb
   A young sheep is a lamb.

15. C — Beef
   Beef comes from cattle.

16. B — Animal hides and skins
   Skins of cattle, goats and sheep become leather.

17. C — Protein
   Protein builds muscles.

18. C — Cooking oil
   Oils give a lot of energy.

19. B — They cook at the same time
   Equal pieces cook evenly.

20. A — Away from your face
   Steam can burn.

21. A — Cool it under running clean water for at least ten minutes
   Cooling reduces burn damage.

22. D — Big bubbles rise quickly and steam comes off
   These are signs of boiling.

23. C — A basin or a soak pit
   To catch the dirty water.

24. D — Soap and clean water
   Soap removes germs.

25. D — So they do not spread dirt and germs
   Dirty tools spread dirt.

26. C — Gloves
   Gloves protect from germs and cuts.

27. A — Cut a jerrican or flat tin
   A cut jerrican forms a scoop.

28. D — Keeping the home and its surroundings clean
   It is care of the home environment.

29. D — Dust mask
   A mask covers the nose and mouth.

30. A — A long stitch followed by a short stitch
   The pattern alternates.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sweep first; fill a bucket with clean soapy water; squeeze the mop; start from the far corner and mop backwards to the door; rinse the mop; leave the floor to dry with a warning.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Washing hands removes germs before they reach the mouth. Safe water and clean food stop germs entering the body. Using the toilet and washing hands afterwards stops germs from spreading.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a ladder or picking pole; do not climb thin branches; wash hands and fruit; use both hands (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: Plastic and glass, because they do not rot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two items, 1 mark for the reason.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Remove laces; brush off loose dirt; scrub gently with soapy water; rinse; stuff with paper; dry in the shade.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Even tacking has equal stitches and gaps; long and short tacking has a long stitch followed by a short stitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each name and 1 for correct descriptions.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example, rice (energy), fish (body-building), spinach (protective).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food correctly named and placed.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: Keeping the home and its surroundings clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for keeping clean, 1 mark for the home.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is thrown away and replaced, not washed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for throwing, 1 mark for replacing.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Big trees such as mango grow slowly and need years before flowering, while pawpaw and passion fruit are small plants that fruit within about a year.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for slow trees, fast plants, and reason of size or type.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Energy-giving: ugali; body-building: beans; protective: sukuma wiki (or other correct examples).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group with example.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: A watering can wets a wide area and much water is lost by running off and by evaporation. Drip irrigation puts water beside the roots slowly, so less is used, fewer weeds grow, and the leaves stay dry.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the watering can, 2 marks for drip irrigation.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fix strong posts about 2 m tall; tie strong wires or strings between them; plant seedlings near the posts; tie the stems gently to the wires.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Its stem is soft and cannot stand, so the trellis supports it as it climbs and spreads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for soft stem, 1 mark for support.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins and minerals, fibre for digestion and water, so they protect the body from disease.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Firewood, charcoal, gas and kerosene.
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each fuel, total 2.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Keeping our own body clean to stay healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for keeping clean, 1 mark for health.
